headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beats Australia by 9 wickets in Darwin
summary: The Tigers achieve their first-ever Test victory on Australian soil, ending a 23-year wait for a win in the region.
details: Bangladesh secured a commanding nine-wicket victory over Australia in the first Test in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.
The Tigers dominated the match across four days, bowling Australia out for 198 in the first innings and maintaining control throughout the game.
Hasan Mahmud led the bowling attack with a six-wicket haul on the opening day, recording the first five-wicket haul by a Bangladeshi bowler in Australia in any format.
Tanzid Tamim shone with a maiden Test century, standing up to Australia's formidable fast bowling attack to build a massive lead.

Every batter contributed, with Mominul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto, and Mushfiqur Rahim providing solid platforms, while Mehidy Hasan Miraz and the tailenders showed grit to secure a 228-run first-innings lead.
Australia was bowled out for 284 in their second innings early on Day 4, leaving Bangladesh to easily chase a small 57-run target to seal the historic win.
BCB chief selector Habibul Bashar noted that the team's determination and hard work paid off, overcoming skepticism from outside the camp.
This victory is a significant milestone for Bangladesh's growth in the longest format of the game, earning them respect as a serious contender in the Test arena.
caption:
A 23-year dream realized! Bangladesh has just made history by defeating Australia in a Test match on their own soil for the first time ever.

Bangladesh secured a commanding nine-wicket victory over Australia in the first Test in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.

The Tigers dominated the match across four days, bowling Australia out for 198 in the first innings and maintaining control throughout the game.

Hasan Mahmud led the bowling attack with a six-wicket haul on the opening day, recording the first five-wicket haul by a Bangladeshi bowler in Australia in any format.

Tanzid Tamim shone with a maiden Test century, standing up to Australia's formidable fast bowling attack to build a massive lead.

Every batter contributed, with Mominul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto, and Mushfiqur Rahim providing solid platforms, while Mehidy Hasan Miraz and the tailenders showed grit to secure a 228-run first-innings lead.

Australia was bowled out for 284 in their second innings early on Day 4, leaving Bangladesh to easily chase a small 57-run target to seal the historic win.

BCB chief selector Habibul Bashar noted that the team's determination and hard work paid off, overcoming skepticism from outside the camp.

This victory is a significant milestone for Bangladesh's growth in the longest format of the game, earning them respect as a serious contender in the Test arena.

headline_marked: 3-0 win: [[Arsenal sweep aside Man City]] to claim Community Shield
headline: 3-0 win: Arsenal sweep aside Man City to claim Community Shield
summary: Captain Martin Odegaard leads the Gunners to a dominant victory in Cardiff, warning rivals that the team wants to 'win everything' this season.
details: Arsenal secured a dominant 3-0 victory over Manchester City in Cardiff on Sunday to lift the Community Shield. Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring after just 24 seconds, followed by a goal from Kai Havertz before half-time.

Captain Martin Odegaard capped off the performance with the final goal and was named man of the match. Following the win, Odegaard warned rivals that the Premier League champions are hungry to 'win everything'.

The match marked a difficult start for Manchester City under new manager Enzo Maresca. The 3-0 defeat is tied for the heaviest loss by a City manager in their first game in charge, matching a result from 1906.
Maresca admitted his side has significant room for improvement before their Premier League opener against Bournemouth on August 24. He noted that conceding so early affected the game's momentum.
Arsenal, the bookmakers' favorites for a second consecutive title, will begin their league campaign at home against promoted Coventry on August 21.
caption:
A 24-second start and a 3-0 demolition. Arsenal just sent a massive warning to the rest of the league!

Arsenal secured a dominant 3-0 victory over Manchester City in Cardiff on Sunday to lift the Community Shield. Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring after just 24 seconds, followed by a goal from Kai Havertz before half-time.

Captain Martin Odegaard capped off the performance with the final goal and was named man of the match. Following the win, Odegaard warned rivals that the Premier League champions are hungry to 'win everything'.

The match marked a difficult start for Manchester City under new manager Enzo Maresca. The 3-0 defeat is tied for the heaviest loss by a City manager in their first game in charge, matching a result from 1906.

Maresca admitted his side has significant room for improvement before their Premier League opener against Bournemouth on August 24. He noted that conceding so early affected the game's momentum.

Arsenal, the bookmakers' favorites for a second consecutive title, will begin their league campaign at home against promoted Coventry on August 21.
